# devicebasedauth.org

> Revocable, device-bound authentication and authorization as a pay-as-you-go web service. A device (browser, phone, server, CLI, AI agent) keeps its own private key; devicebasedauth.org issues it a signed, human-readable credential listing exactly what it may do, on which site, when and where. Servers verify offline for free or ask online (metered) for instant revocation, usage limits and owner approval. Prepaid balance, no subscription.

Machine-readable API: https://devicebasedauth.org/openapi.json
Credential format: https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/credential.md
Grant evaluation rules and test vectors: https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/evaluation.md
Revocation webhook events: https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/events.md
Docs: https://devicebasedauth.org/docs/ (accounts without a password: https://devicebasedauth.org/docs/accounts.html; Android, iOS and TPM devices: https://devicebasedauth.org/docs/devices.html; network rules and address lists: https://devicebasedauth.org/docs/networks.html)
Everything in one file (this summary, every route, the credential spec, evaluation rules and pricing): https://devicebasedauth.org/llms-full.txt
MCP endpoint: POST https://devicebasedauth.org/mcp (Streamable HTTP; Authorization: ApiKey dbak_…, a device credential, or an OAuth access token: MCP clients discover /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp, register at /oauth/register, and the owner approves the scopes)

## Key facts

- Money is integer micro-dollars (µ$; $1 = 1,000,000 µ$). Every JSON response includes `cost_microdollars`. `GET /api/v1/quote?op=<op>` prices an operation before you do it; `?dry_run=1` on a billable call quotes it (and, with `account:read`, says whether the balance covers it) without doing it. Billable responses carry `balance_microdollars` / `X-DBA-Balance-Microdollars` for callers with `account:read`.
- Prices (µ$): issue 87, renew 25, online decision 14, metered API read 7, token exchange or client certificate 7, OIDC login 14 (paid by the site), audience registration/change 100, gate request 22 per gate contacted (webhook gate 23, Duo/Okta Verify 30), confirmation 14, security email 200, named address list create/replace 242 per started 1,000 ranges plus 15 per day it extends the list's published life (13 months ahead). Minimum deposit $5. Offline verification, JWKS, status lists, revocation, inspection and the web dashboard are free.
- Errors: `{ "error": "...", "code": "..." }` with HTTP status; 402 = insufficient balance.
- Private keys never leave the device. The service only ever sees public keys.

## Credentials

A credential is a compact JWS (ES256), header `{"typ":"dba-device+jwt","alg":"ES256","kid":…}`. Decode the middle segment (base64url JSON) to read it:
`iss`, `sub` (device id), `acct` (issuing account), `aud` (site names), `cid` (credential id), `jti`, `iat`/`nbf`/`exp`, `cnf.jkt` (device key thumbprint), `device`, `grants`, `status.status_list {idx, uri}`, `ver` (1, or 2 when any grant has `net`), `confirm` (optional).

A grant: `{ "actions": ["hashbin:content:write"], "resources": ["*"], "when": {"tz","windows":[{"days","from","to"}],"not_before","not_after"}, "where": {"source":"network|device|both","countries","regions","areas":[{"lat","lon","radius_m"}],"networks"}, "limits": {"uses":{"count","per"},"spend_usd_per_month"}, "net": {"client": {"addresses": {"cidrs","lists":[{"id","uri"}],"dns":{"names","dnssec"}},"latency":{"max_rtt_ms","samples","reuse_s"}}}, "require": {"online","step_up","attestation":"hardware|strongbox","verified_boot","app_ids":["TEAMID.bundle.id"],"gates","gates_reuse_s"} }`. Deny by default; any passing grant allows; unknown constraints deny.

Present it as `Authorization: DBA <credential>` plus `DPoP: <proof>` (RFC 9449 proof JWT signed by the device key with htm, htu, iat, jti, ath). For the first minute after an account's server object starts, devicebasedauth.org answers proofs without its nonce with `401 use_dpop_nonce` and the nonce in the `DPoP-Nonce` header (also `dpop_nonce` in the body): make a new proof with the `nonce` claim and send once more (the browser SDK v1.4.0+ and the CLI do this). Clients that cannot send twice get the nonce first from `POST /api/v1/dpop-nonce` (free).

## Verify (relying party)

```js
import { createVerifier } from '@devicebasedauth/verify';
const dba = createVerifier({ audience: 'example.com' });
const result = await dba.verifyRequest(request, { action: 'example:write', resource: 'doc-1' });
if (!result.allow) return new Response(result.code, { status: result.status });
// Grants with usage limits / step-up / require.online: dba.verifyOnline(request, check) with createVerifier({ online: { apiKey } }).
```

Offline verification fetches `https://devicebasedauth.org/.well-known/jwks.json` and status lists (`https://status.devicebasedauth.org/v1/lists/<n>`, signed JWT, bit idx set = revoked), caching both.

Instant offline revocation: set `revocation_webhook` (https on your audience's domain) with `PATCH /api/v1/audiences/{name}`. Revocations of credentials naming your audience arrive as a POSTed JWS (`typ: dba-event+jwt`, signed with the issuer key); `await dba.handleEvent(await request.text())` verifies it and makes the verifier deny those credentials at once. Retried after 1 min, 10 min, 1 h; free for audiences; the status list stays authoritative. `POST /api/v1/audiences/{name}/webhook-test` sends a test event (read price).

## Accounts (no password or sign-in provider needed)

- An account is created by paying its first deposit ($5–$20 in the first week) with a new device key; Clerk sign-in is optional. Browser: https://devicebasedauth.org/signup.html, or SDK v1.3.0 `await dba.signUp({ creditCents: 500, acceptTerms: true })` → send the person to `url` (Stripe Checkout) → `await dba.finish()`. CLI: `dba signup --accept-terms` (prints a recovery sheet). HTTP: `POST /api/v1/signup {request (dba-enroll+jwt, aud/grants optional), credit_cents, accept_terms: true}` → `{url, account, ticket}`; after payment `POST /api/v1/signup/complete {ticket}` with a DPoP proof by the key (ath = hash of the ticket) returns `pending`, then the `dba:session` credential. Stores nothing until Stripe's signed webhook arrives.
- For 10 minutes after sign-up or recovery the device counts as recently signed in. Later, operations that need a recent sign-in (API keys, `dba:*` credentials, gates, recovery codes, raised limits) need `POST /api/v1/session/reverify`: one of the owner's passkey, security-key, authenticator-app or other-device gates approves (403 `reverification_required` says so).
- Getting back in after losing every device (free): `POST /api/v1/recover {account, via: "code", code, request}` (at once), `{account, via: "gate", request}` (a passkey or another device approves, typing the returned `number`), or `{email, via: "email", request}` (link to an address verified with `POST /api/v1/account/email`; then a 72-hour wait any signed-in device can cancel). Finish gate and email recoveries with `POST /api/v1/recover/complete {ticket}` + DPoP. CLI: `dba recover --account acct_… --code …` / `--via gate` / `--email …`, `--resume`. `GET /api/v1/account/recovery` lists the ways back in.
- A password (Clerk) sign-in can be linked to such an account and removed: `POST`/`DELETE /api/v1/account/clerk-link`.

## Enroll a device

- Browser: `import { DBA } from 'https://devicebasedauth.org/sdk/dba.js'; const dba = new DBA(); await dba.enroll({ aud: ['example.com'], grants: [{ actions: ['example:write'] }] }); await dba.fetch(url)`.
- CLI / agent: `dba enroll --aud example.com --action example:write` prints an approval URL for the human owner, then polls. `dba curl …`, `dba token --aud example.com`, `dba renew`, `dba revoke`, `dba list` (the account's credentials; `DBA_API_KEY` with `credentials:read`, or a device holding `dba:credentials:read`). The CLI renews automatically at 2/3 of the lifetime when it uses the credential (`--no-renew` or `DBA_AUTO_RENEW=0` to stop); `dba renew --if-due` suits cron.
- HTTP: `POST /api/v1/enrollments {request}` where request is a JWS (typ `dba-enroll+jwt`, the new public key in the header `jwk`) over `{iat, aud, grants, device, lifetime_seconds?}`. Response: `approval_url` (give it to the human), `poll_url`. Poll `GET poll_url` until `status` is `approved` (then `credential` is included), `denied` or `expired`.
- Android key attestation (optional): `POST /api/v1/enrollments/attestation-challenge` → `challenge`; generate the Keystore key with `setAttestationChallenge(challenge ASCII bytes)`; add `attestation: {format: "android-key", challenge, x5c: [base64 DER, leaf first]}` to the enrollment request payload. Verified chains put `device.attestation {format, security_level: tee|strongbox, verified_boot, device_locked, verified_at}` in the credential; a rejected chain is `400 invalid_attestation`. Sample: docs/samples/android.
- Apple App Attest (optional): same challenge; make the key in the Secure Enclave, then `attestKey(keyId, clientDataHash: SHA-256("<challenge>.<JWK thumbprint>"))` and add `attestation: {format: "apple-appattest", challenge, app_id: "TEAMID.bundle.id", key_id, object}` (base64). Gives `device.attestation {format, security_level: secure_enclave, app_id, environment}`; it satisfies `require.attestation` only for production builds of apps listed in `require.app_ids` (Apple attests the app, not the key).
- TPM 2.0 attestation (optional, Windows): same challenge; create the P-256 key in the TPM, `TPM2_Certify` it with the AIK using qualifyingData `SHA-256("<challenge>.<JWK thumbprint>")`, and add `attestation: {format: "tpm", challenge, alg: -257|-65535, x5c: [AIK cert, CA certs], sig, cert_info, pub_area}` (base64). The AIK chain must end at the Microsoft TPM Root CA 2014. Gives `device.attestation {format, security_level: tpm, tpm_manufacturer}`, which satisfies `require.attestation: "hardware"`.
- TPM 2.0 without a Microsoft AIK certificate (Linux): EK credential activation. `POST /api/v1/enrollments/tpm-activation` with `{challenge, ek_certificate (RSA-2048 EK cert, NV 0x01c00002), ek_chain?, ak_pub_area (restricted signing AK), pub_area, cert_info, sig (TPMT_SIGNATURE)}`; the EK cert must chain to a TPM manufacturer's EK CA. Unwrap the returned `credential_blob` (tpm2_activatecredential format; or `id_object` + `encrypted_secret`) with TPM2_ActivateCredential and enroll with `attestation: {format: "tpm-ek", challenge, activation, secret}` within 10 minutes. Same resulting claim.
- Fleets: the owner creates an enrollment token (`POST /api/v1/enrollment-tokens {name, aud, grants, lifetime_seconds, max_uses, expires_in_days}` → `token: dbae_…`, shown once). Each device signs its usual enrollment request (aud/grants optional; may only narrow the token's) and sends `POST /api/v1/enrollments/redeem {request, enrollment_token}` — issued at once, issue price charged to the token's account. CLI: `DBA_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN=dbae_… dba enroll`; SDK: `dba.enroll({}, { enrollmentToken })`.
- mTLS: `POST /api/v1/certificate {lifetime_seconds?}` (device credential + DPoP; 300–86400 s, default 3600; token price) returns a PEM X.509 client certificate for the device's own key, signed by the CA in `/.well-known/dba-ca.pem`; CN = device id, SAN URIs `urn:devicebasedauth:{device,credential,account}:…`; no grants, no revocation. CLI: `dba certificate` then `curl --cert client.crt --key client.key`.
- Pre-approved issuance: `POST /api/v1/credentials {public_jwk, aud, grants, device, lifetime_seconds}` with an API key holding `credentials:issue` (or a device credential holding `dba:credentials:issue`, which can only delegate narrower grants to its own audiences or fewer, one level deep: a delegated credential cannot delegate again, `403 delegation_depth`). An API key can grant `dba:` actions only within its own scopes.

## Gates (approvals) and periodic confirmation

- Gates approve uses of a grant: `require.gates: [{ any: [gate ids or "owner"], timeout_s?, on_timeout?: "deny"|"allow" }]` (1–3 entries, all must pass), `require.gates_reuse_s`. Kinds: owner, dba-device, totp, webauthn, webhook, duo, okta-verify. Manage with `GET|POST /api/v1/gates`, `DELETE /api/v1/gates/{id}`, `POST /api/v1/gates/{id}/test` (webhook gates; read price) (scopes `gates:read`, `gates:write`; changing needs a recent sign-in or an API key). CLI: `dba gates`, `dba gates add --kind dba-device|webhook`.
- Online only: `/authorize` answers `gate_pending` with `gate_request: {id, retry_after, deadline}` until the gates settle, then allows or `gate_denied`. Sites pass it on as 403; devices retry (SDK `fetchWithGates()`, CLI `dba curl --dba-wait`).
- A device holding `dba:approvals:answer` answers as a dba-device gate: `GET /api/v1/gate-requests` (each item's `answer_as: [{entry, gate}]`), `POST /api/v1/gate-requests/{id}/answer {entry, gate, decision: "allow"|"deny", number?}`. CLI: `dba approvals [--watch]`, `dba approvals allow|deny ID`.
- Webhook gates: DBA POSTs a `dba-gate+jwt` to your service; answer `{"decision"}` at once or 202 then a signed `dba-gate-answer+jwt` to `callback` (spec/events.md §6).
- Periodic confirmation: credentials issued with `confirm: {gates, every_s}` need a current `dba-confirmation+jwt` sent as `DBA-Confirmation`; get one with `POST /api/v1/credentials/{cid}/confirm` (retry while `pending`). CLI `dba confirm`; SDK `confirm()`. `POST /api/v1/credentials/{cid}/unconfirm` stops trust online at once.
- Audiences may require gates per catalog action (`catalog[].gates: {require, kinds, fail_open}`) and for sign-in (`sign_in_gates`).

## Network rules and named address lists

- A grant's `net.client` limits the connection (spec/evaluation.md §3.10; credential `ver` 2, so older verifiers deny it): `addresses` allow the peer address when it is in `cidrs` (1–64), in a named address list (`lists`, 1–8 `{id, uri}`), or equal to an A/AAAA address of `dns.names` (with `dnssec: true` only validated answers count); `latency.max_rtt_ms` bounds the round trip, measured by a timed DPoP nonce challenge. Verifiers evaluate only `client`; `net.server`, `route` and `addresses.webhook` are in the format but nothing supplies or enforces them yet. Reasons: `address_unavailable`, `address_not_allowed` (+ `address_list_unavailable:<id>`, `dns_unresolved:<name>`, `dns_unvalidated:<name>`), `rtt_required`, `rtt_exceeded`.
- Verifier: `createVerifier({ audience, rtt: { secret }, dns: true })`; lists are fetched and cached by default (60 s fresh, 10 min stale, no rollback). A latency grant first answers `401 use_dpop_nonce`: send `result.headers` and `rtt: result.rtt` so the device retries. The unversioned browser SDK (`/sdk/dba.js`) answers timed challenges; `dba headers`/`sign`/`curl` cannot and refuse credentials whose every grant is timed.
- Named address lists (up to 10,000 IPv4/IPv6 ranges, 50 per account): `GET|POST /api/v1/address-lists {name, cidrs}`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/address-lists/{id}` (scopes `networks:read`, `networks:write`; replace and delete need a recent sign-in or an API key). Each is published signed (`dba-addresses+jwt`) at `https://status.devicebasedauth.org/v1/addresses/{id}` within about a minute; a grant names it by `id` and that exact `uri`, and only the issuing account's live lists are accepted (`400 unknown_address_list`). Unchanged for 13 months, a list expires; deleted, it matches nothing. Grants with `dba:` actions cannot use lists yet.

## Main endpoints

- `GET /api/v1/whoami` — who is calling.
- `GET /api/v1/credentials`, `GET /api/v1/credentials/{cid}` (grants in plain English), `DELETE /api/v1/credentials/{cid}` (revoke), `GET /api/v1/credentials/{cid}/decisions`.
- `GET /api/v1/devices`, `POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/revoke`, `POST /api/v1/revoke-all {"confirm":"revoke-all"}`.
- `POST /api/v1/credentials/{cid}/renew` (device credential + DPoP; `new_key_proof` to rotate keys; also free recovery of a credential whose issuer key was withdrawn, after which other APIs answer 401 `reissue_required`), `POST /api/v1/token {audience}` (≤10-minute bearer token), `POST /api/v1/self/revoke`.
- `POST /api/v1/authorize {credential, proof, request:{method,url}, audience, action, resource, context:{network}}` — online decision for an audience you own.
- `POST /api/v1/inspect {credential, check?}` — decode, verify, check revocation, evaluate. Free.
- `GET|POST /api/v1/audiences` — relying parties and their action catalogs (`GET /api/v1/audiences/{name}/usage`: your audience's online decisions, sign-ins and spend per month); register your domain (prove it with `https://<domain>/.well-known/devicebasedauth.json` = `{"account":"<your account>"}`).
- `GET /api/v1/account`, `GET /api/v1/transactions`, `GET /api/v1/audit`, `GET|PATCH /api/v1/account/settings` (dashboard only: `max_issues_per_day`, default 500; `max_renewals_per_credential_per_month`, default no cap; beyond them the API answers 429 `issuance_limit` / `renewal_limit` and charges nothing; `security_email`: `all` (default), `sensitive` or `off` — takeover-sensitive events are emailed at once, other issuances in at most one digest an hour, each email charged the `notice` price when queued; raising a limit or turning emails down needs a recent sign-in).
- OpenID Connect: `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (authorization code + PKCE S256; client_id = audience name).

## API keys and scopes

Create keys in the dashboard (`dbak_…`, shown once). Scopes: `account:read`, `transactions:read`, `credentials:read`, `credentials:issue`, `credentials:revoke`, `audiences:read`, `audiences:write`, `authorize`, `networks:read`, `networks:write`, `gates:read`, `gates:write` (`approvals:answer` is for devices only). Send `Authorization: ApiKey dbak_…`. Key reads are metered (read price, 7 µ$); dashboard reads are free.

## First-party audiences

`devicebasedauth.org` (namespace `dba`), `hashbin.org` (`hashbin:*`, mirrors hashbin's API key scopes, e.g. `hashbin:content:write`), `cronly.org` (`cronly:read`, `cronly:run`, `cronly:change`, `cronly:prose`, `cronly:secrets:write`), `subetha.us` (`subetha:publish`, `subetha:subscribe`; resources are topic names or `@handle/*`). `<ns>:session` means "may sign in to that site". `GET /api/v1/audiences` lists every catalog.
